name: Gweike G2 Pro 30W Fiber
tagline: 30W Desktop fiber marker for metal and select plastics
tldr: Gweike G2 Pro 30W Fiber is the 30W SKU on the Gweike gweike g2 line. Gweike G2 packages a 20W fiber galvo in a desktop form factor. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Entry fiber marking on small metal parts

priceRange.note: Official Gweike store, Oct 2026: $1,599 to $1,799 depending on manual or electric lift

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

pros: Two configurations: 110 mm lens with manual lift at $1,599, or 150 mm lens with electric lift at $1,799 (Gweike, Oct 2026)
About 75% deeper than the 20W in Gweike's two-hour brass test (3.7 mm vs 2.1 mm)
Cuts 0.5 mm brass in about 7 passes at 10 mm/s, workable for small jewelry blanks
cons: Still a Q-switched source: no MOPA pulse control for consistent colours on stainless
In the 150 mm electric version, the price gap to the G2 Max is only $700
Millimetre-deep engraving still takes hours, not minutes

faq.question: What does the G2 Pro 30W gain over the 20W in practice?
faq.answer: Mostly depth and fewer passes. In Gweike's comparison the 30W reached about 3.7 mm in brass after two hours at 1,000 mm/s (20W: 2.1 mm) and 2.3 mm in slate after one hour (20W: 1.7 mm). It cut 0.5 mm brass in 7 passes at 10 mm/s, against 11 for the 20W. Surface marks look much the same.

faq.question: How much does the G2 Pro 30W cost compared with the other G2 models?
faq.answer: On Gweike's US store (October 2026) the G2 Pro is $1,599 with the 110 mm lens and manual lift, or $1,799 with the 150 mm lens and electric lift. That is $300 to $450 more than the 20W in the same configuration, and $700 less than the G2 Max, which only comes with the 150 mm lens and electric lift at $2,499.

faq.question: G2 Pro or G2 Max: which one for a small engraving business?
faq.answer: The Pro suits a business that mostly marks: tumblers, pet tags, knives, business cards, with some deeper engraving now and then. Pick the Max if coins, deep relief or cutting thin brass and silver blanks are weekly jobs: in Gweike's demo it cuts 0.5 mm brass in 4 passes instead of 7.

standoutFeatures.title: A clear depth step over the 20W
standoutFeatures.body: Gweike's comparison shows 3.7 mm in brass after two hours at 1,000 mm/s, against 2.1 mm for the 20W. Coins, dog tags with deep text and slate reach the same result in noticeably fewer passes.

standoutFeatures.title: Choice of 110 mm or 150 mm field
standoutFeatures.body: The Pro is sold with either lens. The 110 mm lens gives a smaller spot for fine text; the 150 mm lens fits more parts per batch. The G2 Max only ships with the 150 mm lens.

beginnerNotes: This profile is the 30W SKU on Gweike G2 Pro Fiber. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Fix parts firmly; start with low power test squares on scrap metal. Rotary adds complexity: budget time to learn indexing.
primaryUse: Desktop fiber marking for jewelry-scale and test jobs

editorialDepth.advantages: Gweike G2 Pro Fiber 30W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom (50W) or a different machine class.
